workstreams.name: Core analysis and visualizer workflow
workstreams.basis: Imports, provider execution, stored code units, source navigation, and review workflows exist. The profiler recognizes structurally plausible PyInstaller CArchive cookies in native executables and records package/runtime metadata. A pinned, MIT-licensed pyinstxtractor-go snapshot now runs in a bounded isolated service, extracts capped Python bytecode children, persists each accepted child as a task-scoped derived artifact and database code unit, and feeds up to four not-yet-decompiled modules per run to pycdc while skipping exact-hash modules already completed in prior project runs; child records retain executable, archive-path, extractor-revision, bytecode-hash, and recovered-source provenance. The Go image builds and webapp type-checks; representative archive execution and fidelity validation remain open. The Python bytecode workflow pairs hash-verified recovered source with bounded bytecode in the visualizer and MCP dossier, keeps module-wide evidence out of selected-function context, and carries the raw bytecode magic without inferring a runtime version. Native Mach-O analysis stores exact-address Swift/Objective-C metadata and exposes capped, hash-checked ReIPA pseudocode alternatives; the visualizer can compare native provider outputs by canonical function identity across differing saved paths and output-language labels. Isolated pinned Glaurung, Kuna, and Fission providers persist bounded native C-like pseudocode; Fission's exact-hash per-function outputs are included as same-function AI context only after binary-hash, identity, completed-run, and output-hash checks. Kuna also stores assembly, selected call/jump/reference edges, and bounded opcode sequences. A pinned isolated Recurse MCP adapter stores bounded per-function VTIL-style lift evidence and optimizer counters, displayed with its semantic limits; container build, runtime, and fixture comparison remain open. The visualizer and rewrite context compare Ghidra/Kuna instruction sequences across providers only when normalized architecture groups agree, exclude same-function cross-provider self-matches, and keep provider, analysis-run, artifact-hash, identity, and similarity provenance with reused names. Kuna's v1.878 analyzer image and end-to-end worker have been exercised against a system ELF binary. A read-only Ghidra p-code emulator also persists bounded, confidence-labeled control-flow-flattening transitions as visualizer navigation evidence. Ghidra now offers separate opt-in pinned BcfClean and CffDeflatten passes with bounded scans, emulation audits, and hash-checked alternatives in the visualizer and rewrite context; runtime and representative fixture comparisons remain open. The new Fission adapter still needs image-build, runtime, and fixture comparison. Newly settled decompile/disassemble tasks now persist a centralized coverage inventory after database ingestion, separating provider-discovered, provider-returned, raw-observed, and indexed units, along with the unaccounted remainder, not-observed and not-indexed counts, truncation, and classifications the provider reported. The visualizer uses the stored inventory and labels older runs without it. TypeScript type-check and targeted ESLint pass; provider coverage and runtime behavior remain to be exercised, and unsupported/skip/exclusion classifications remain unknown when engines do not report them.

workstreams.name: Database-grounded project memory and provenance
workstreams.basis: Project-scoped observations, symbols, relationships, drafts, and review records ground AI context. Common native virtual-address spellings now canonicalize across Ghidra, Glaurung, and Oxidizer for same-artifact function identity; bounded same-binary, completed-run lookups bring accepted cross-provider names into rewrite, explanation, and MCP dossier contexts for selected units with canonical-key or normalized native-identity matches, exact input-hash checks, and review-receipt verification. Ghidra/Kuna lookalike context now retains the producing provider, analysis task, artifact identity and hash, normalized architecture, native function identity, and similarity score; opening an older match resolves its exact completed run only within the active project artifact selection. Fission, Ghidra, and Kuna same-function native reconstructions can now enter selected-unit rewrite context only when the input artifact hash, canonical address identity, completed provider run, and saved output hash all match; each is labeled provisional provider evidence. Recurse VTIL-style lift artifacts persist exact input/output hashes, provider revision, native function identity, and optimizer counters; rewrite context reads a same-function lift only from a completed run with exact input, identity, run-path, and output-hash checks, while labeling the lift as provisional structural evidence. Legacy native address aliases remain a fallback and are labeled separately because they can denote thunks. MCP provider outputs also require exact input and saved-output hashes; accepted project-memory lookup is bounded to 100 candidate provider observations and reports possible truncation. Exact-address ReIPA pseudocode alternatives for matched Swift/Objective-C methods enter rewrite context and MCP dossiers only after same-run provenance checks. Ghidra functions persist bounded basic-block/edge/entry/exit metrics and a bounded basic-block graph for the visualizer. Control-flow-flattening recovery now persists in function observation attributes and is available to the visualizer, rewrite/explanation, and MCP dossier as confidence-labeled structural evidence; it does not establish identity or behavior. Opt-in BcfClean and CffDeflatten pseudocode enters rewrite context only after the pinned provider version, same-artifact hash, exact address, saved-output hash, and successful emulation audit all match. The MCP code dossier now recomputes maintained-source and saved-draft hashes before exposing their code or validator results; Python bytecode units now retain hashes for both reconstructed source and disassembly, and the visualizer, MCP dossier, and module-level rewrite context verify those hashes; module-wide bytecode evidence is withheld from selected-function context unless a unique same-module code-object name match exists; maintained code also requires an accepted receipt matching the exact source bytes. Rewrite context now reads accepted symbols from immutable receipt snapshots and rehashes maintained callee source before using it. The visualizer and Ghidra export use the accepted receipt’s same symbol snapshot for historical rename names, lineage, and address annotations. Broader identity coverage and fixture validation remain open. PyInstaller bytecode children now persist as task-scoped derived artifacts with database code-unit records linking each module to the executable hash, archive member, extractor revision, and bytecode hash; up to four selected modules gain hash-verified pycdc source provenance, while remaining modules retain bytecode evidence for later review. PyInstaller selection now queries prior project observations using the exact executable hash and stable module code-unit key, so repeated runs continue through pending modules instead of restarting the same four-module batch. Scope-safe rename proposals are persisted as proposal-only attempts with the exact editable source and hash, accepted project-symbol context and hash, provider/model, and mappings; applied attempts link to that proposal and verify selected mappings against it. Attempt history displays and reloads saved proposals only after the current source hash and provider match. Prior proposals enter later AI prompts as unreviewed hints, never accepted evidence. TypeScript type-check, targeted ESLint, and Python AST parsing pass; runtime workflow and fixture evidence remain pending.

workstreams.name: Major-language and format decompilation fluency
workstreams.basis: Several useful Java, .NET, Android, Python, WebAssembly, and native paths exist, and matched arm64 Mach-O methods can now show early ReIPA C-like pseudocode beside Ghidra output; optional Glaurung and Kuna providers add bounded native C-like pseudocode, with Kuna also saving assembly and selected graph edges. Kuna's analyzer has built and completed an end-to-end system-ELF smoke run, but both native alternates still need representative fixture comparison and fidelity validation. Many languages remain navigation-only, early, or represented by generic pseudocode. The new isolated Arlecchino provider builds from its audited upstream revision, combines Vineflower, CFR, and JADX per class using compiler-error ranking, and stores canonical rename provenance, round-trip coverage, and hash-attributed output. Runtime and fixture fidelity remain unverified, so this adds a limited early JVM capability only. The pycdc provider stores a hash-attributed recovered Python source artifact and bounded bytecode disassembly, both linked to Python source units and verified by the visualizer. Selected-function context can include an exact-run code-object section when one matching name exists in the module, while ambiguous matches are omitted; module context retains the bounded full listing. A bounded isolated PyInstaller extractor now sends recovered `.pyc` members through that provider and preserves executable, archive-member, bytecode, and source hashes; only image-build and type-check evidence exist so far, so execution and source fidelity remain unvalidated. The ILSpy provider now applies a pinned NoFuserEx static ConfuserEx cleanup subset before decompilation, stores transformed assemblies separately with exact input/output hashes and pass provenance, and labels the output as intermediate; the image builds, while fixture-backed fidelity remains open. The webcrack analyzer also recovers embedded JavaScript/TypeScript from bounded local version 3 source maps, storing exact map and content provenance; maps are optional build evidence and may be stale, so broad TypeScript bundle reconstruction remains open. The isolated ILSpy analyzer now emits bounded, syntax-parsed Visual Basic-shaped translations from its C# reconstruction with exact source/output hashes and pinned CodeConverter provenance; this is an early bridge only, not recovered original VB, and fixture compilation and behavior checks remain open. A constrained CRuby 3.4.11 provider recognizes YARB ISeq artifacts and stores bounded raw disassembly plus a hash-verified structured sequence/opcode tree with locals, parameters, catch entries, opcode operands, and an early label-derived CFG. A bounded BSD-2-Clause Ruby 2.7-focused adapter now creates an experimental source candidate as a separate artifact when it passes CRuby 3.4.11 syntax parsing; the upstream is version-mismatched, so syntax acceptance does not establish behavior or fidelity. Vineflower now integrates the pinned Apache-2.0 Java Deobfuscator static Allatori flow pass for bounded JARs and stores a separate transformed artifact plus alternate sources when supported patterns are found; target code is not run, and behavior/fidelity comparison remains open. Static checks and image builds are still required for this latest slice.

workstreams.name: Maintainable editing, review, and export
workstreams.basis: Hash-bound drafts and review receipts preserve exact source lineage. New accepted reviews snapshot the exact source and symbol index; the visualizer can restore a verified prior source into a new review using that revision's saved rename context. Accepted-source promotion rejects failed or unavailable validation and prevents a previously accepted language-specific syntax check from silently downgrading to generic Tree-sitter evidence. An initial JVM rebuild path compiles one receipt-verified accepted Java class against the original JAR in the isolated JDK analyzer, patches matching class entries into a separate unsigned derived JAR, removes stale nested class files, and records the input/source/output hashes and compiler version in project observations. This is single-class build evidence only: signed and multi-release JARs, external dependency classpaths, cross-file builds, and runtime/fixture validation remain open. Syntax-aware edits cover selected languages, with reproducible export; the visualizer now exposes hash-pinned Phpactor LSP local-variable and parameter renames for PHP, validates rewritten source with PHP lint, and records the rename engine, mappings, and hashes in the existing reviewable attempt flow. This first integration is single-file and has container image-build, compile, and type-check evidence; runtime rename smoke checks, fixture coverage, project-wide PHP symbols, and behavior checks remain open. Broad language coverage and project-level edits remain limited. Saved rename proposals can be reviewed after reload and restored into the editor only when their source hash and provider still match; applying them remains a separate reviewed action. The proposal stage is explicitly marked unvalidated, and the resulting scope-aware transformation keeps its syntax/binding validation record and proposal lineage. Type-check and targeted lint pass; runtime rename fixtures remain open.

workstreams.name: Fixture-backed validation and fidelity evidence
workstreams.basis: Provider smoke checks and structural validators exist, but broad versioned clean, optimized, stripped, and obfuscated fixture comparisons are still missing.
